title: Composite Route–Orbital Symmetry for a Charged-Fermion Mass Plane in an SU(15)p Preon Theory: Microscopic Operators, a Minimal Anomaly-Safe Completion, and Decisive Six-Channel Spectral Tests
content: We investigate whether an anomaly-free chiral preon theory can provide a microscopic origin for a simple regularity among the nine charged-fermion Yukawa eigenvalues. The three sectors are charged leptons (e, μ, τ), down-type quarks (d, s, b), and up-type quarks (u, c, t), labelled by $s=\ell,d,u$. For eigenvalues $y_{s,g}(\mu)$ of generation $g=1,2,3$, renormalized in one scheme at one common scale $\mu$, define the dimensionless logarithmic curvature \begin{equation} A_s(\mu)=\frac14\ln\!\left[\frac{y_{s,1}(\mu)y_{s,3}(\mu)}{y_{s,2}^2(\mu)}\right]. \end{equation} It is one quarter of the second finite difference of $\ln y_{s,g}$ and vanishes for an exact geometric progression. The phenomenological target is \begin{equation} \Delta_\Pi(\mu)\equiv A_\ell(\mu)+2A_d(\mu)-A_u(\mu)=0. \end{equation} Current common-scale central values lie near this plane, but their correlated uncertainties do not establish an exact zero. The plane is therefore a falsifiable target for a mechanism, not an empirical law assumed in advance. In a fixed composite-operator basis the normal displacement reduces exactly to \begin{equation} \Delta_\Pi=C_{21}^{\rm match}-C_{12}^{\rm match},\end{equation} where $C_{12}^{\rm match}$ and $C_{21}^{\rm match}$ are renormalized Wilson coefficients of two crossed composite operators. The labels 12 and 21 refer to two internal preon/Wilson-line connectivities, called routes; they are not generation labels. The mass-plane problem is thereby converted into the dynamical question of whether the matching covector is route-even. Starting from the published $SU(15)_p$ precolor theory, we construct an explicit gauge-invariant point-split 24-preon interpolator and prove that its two reflected route sources remain linearly independent after the local Schouten, Fierz, Fermi-statistics, and representation quotient. A route reflection $\tau$, $\tau^2=1$, produces a one-dimensional odd operator line $\tau\mathcal L_-=-\mathcal L_-$. The natural Fierz two-complex $X_6$ of six undaggered $\Omega FF$ junctions satisfies \(\pi_1(X_6)=0\) and \(H^1(X_6;\mathbb Z)=0\): local recouplings remove the large graph-cycle degeneracy, while a route-reflection orbifold sign can survive as a separate structure. These are exact source and topology statements; neither establishes the ordering of physical bound states. The unmodified multiplicity-one theory encounters a sharper algebraic obstruction. Ordinary published Wilson transport acts trivially on the four-dimensional primitive fiber, and Schur-diagonal crossed kernels cannot simultaneously preserve the required odd line and generate a nonzero route splitting. We prove that at least one additional real same-irrep amplitude is required in each of the three inequivalent channels (03,150,153). A minimal orbital/vectorlike completion saturates this lower bound without changing the confining group or its chiral anomaly balance. Its exact same-irrep involution $\mathcal X_{\rm orb}$ permits the whitened route kernel \begin{equation} \widetilde K_{\rm route}=\alpha\mathbf1_2+\beta\sigma_x, \qquad \beta\ne0, \end{equation} so exact odd-line closure coexists with a generic even–odd splitting. The remaining physical problem is formulated through the renormalized 6 × 6 Euclidean correlator. The Ward identity generated by $\mathcal X_{\rm orb}$ reduces it exactly to independent even and odd 3 × 3 generalized eigenvalue problems. We derive the covariant route-residue weights $R_+(E_\star)$ and $R_-(E_\star)$ below a predeclared energy boundary $E_\star$. Two route-visible low-energy spectral directions exist if and only if both weights are nonzero; for one isolated pole per parity this becomes $z_+z_-\ne0$. A constructive no-identifiability theorem shows that symmetry, positivity, anomaly cancellation, and the algebraic kernel do not determine these residues or the sign of $\Delta E=E_{-,0}-E_{+,0}$. Moreover, finite-volume levels must be separated from genuine bound-state or resonance poles. The final test therefore requires a continuum and volume-controlled six-channel ensemble, followed by an independent three-point matching function whose route-odd component vanishes. No nonperturbative energy or residue is invented. The result is not yet a first-principles mass formula; it is a minimal, anomaly-consistent mechanism with an explicit sequence of measurements that can confirm or falsify the proposed origin of the charged-fermion mass plane. The neutrino extension remains conditional on the Majorana sector and is not used in the charged-sector proof.
